title: 69. Numeracy & Number Systems: Greatest Common Divisor
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the greatest common divisor and use it to identify the largest common factor or piece length.
questions.question: What is the greatest common divisor of \(12\) and \(18\)?
questions.explanation: The positive divisors of \(12\) are \(1\), \(2\), \(3\), \(4\), \(6\), \(12\). The positive divisors of \(18\) are \(1\), \(2\), \(3\), \(6\), \(9\), \(18\). The greatest number appearing in both lists is \(6\). Therefore, the greatest common divisor of \(12\) and \(18\) is \(6\). The alternative \(9\) is not a divisor of every given integer.
questions.hint: List the positive divisors of each number and find the largest shared divisor.

questions.concept: GCD of a Power of Two and a Multiple
questions.learningObjective: Determine the greatest common divisor and use it to identify the largest common factor or piece length.
questions.question: What is the greatest common divisor of \(16\) and \(24\)?
questions.explanation: Write \(16=2^4\) and \(24=2^3\times 3\). The common prime factor is \(2\), and the smallest power of \(2\) appearing in both factorizations is \(2^3=8\). Therefore, the greatest common divisor is \(8\). The alternative \(4\) is a smaller common divisor, so it is not the greatest one.
questions.hint: Use prime factorization and take the lowest power of each common prime factor.

questions.concept: GCD with Two Shared Prime Factors
questions.learningObjective: Determine the greatest common divisor and use it to identify the largest common factor or piece length.
questions.question: What is the greatest common divisor of \(36\) and \(48\)?
questions.explanation: Write \(36=2^2\times 3^2\) and \(48=2^4\times 3\). The common prime factors are \(2\) and \(3\). Taking the lowest power of each common prime factor gives \(2^2\times 3=4\times 3=12\). Therefore, the greatest common divisor is \(12\). The alternative \(6\) is a smaller common divisor, so it is not the greatest one.
questions.hint: Find the common prime factors and use the smallest exponent for each.

questions.concept: Lowest Shared Prime Powers in a GCD
questions.learningObjective: Determine the greatest common divisor and use it to identify the largest common factor or piece length.
questions.question: What is the greatest common divisor of \(42\) and \(56\)?
questions.explanation: Write \(42=2^1\times 3\times 7^1\) and \(56=2^3\times 7^1\). For the greatest common divisor, take the lowest power of each common prime: \(2^1\times 7^1=14\). The value \(7\) omits the common factor \(2\).
questions.hint: Compare prime factorizations and retain the lowest exponent of each shared prime.

questions.concept: GCD of Two Multiples of Five
questions.learningObjective: Determine the greatest common divisor and use it to identify the largest common factor or piece length.
questions.question: What is the greatest common divisor of \(45\) and \(75\)?
questions.explanation: Write \(45=3^2\times 5\) and \(75=3\times 5^2\). The common prime factors are \(3\) and \(5\). Taking the lowest power of each gives \(3\times 5=15\). Therefore, the greatest common divisor is \(15\). The alternative \(5\) is a smaller common divisor, so it is not the greatest one.
questions.hint: Factor each number into primes and multiply the common prime factors with the smallest exponents.

questions.concept: GCD with Three Shared Prime Factors
questions.learningObjective: Determine the greatest common divisor and use it to identify the largest common factor or piece length.
questions.question: What is the greatest common divisor of \(84\) and \(126\)?
questions.explanation: Write \(84=2^2\times 3\times 7\) and \(126=2\times 3^2\times 7\). The common prime factors are \(2\), \(3\), and \(7\). Taking the lowest power of each gives \(2\times 3\times 7=42\). Therefore, the greatest common divisor is \(42\). The alternative \(21\) is a smaller common divisor, so it is not the greatest one.
questions.hint: For each shared prime, compare the exponents before forming their product.

questions.concept: Comparing Unequal Prime Exponents for a GCD
questions.learningObjective: Determine the greatest common divisor and use it to identify the largest common factor or piece length.
questions.question: What is the greatest common divisor of \(72\) and \(120\)?
questions.explanation: Write \(72=2^3\times 3^2\) and \(120=2^3\times 3\times 5\). The common prime factors are \(2\) and \(3\). The smallest power of \(2\) is \(2^3\), and the smallest power of \(3\) is \(3\). Their product is \(2^3\times 3=8\times 3=24\). Therefore, the greatest common divisor is \(24\). The alternative \(12\) is a smaller common divisor, so it is not the greatest one.
questions.hint: Use the prime factorization method and select the lowest exponent for each shared prime.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the greatest common divisor and use it to identify the largest common factor or piece length.
questions.question: What is the greatest common divisor of \(18\), \(24\), and \(30\)?
questions.explanation: Write \(18=2\times 3^2\), \(24=2^3\times 3\), and \(30=2\times 3\times 5\). The common prime factors are \(2\) and \(3\). Taking the lowest power of each gives \(2\times 3=6\). Therefore, the greatest common divisor is \(6\). The alternative \(12\) is not a divisor of every given integer.
questions.hint: Find the prime factors common to all three numbers.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the greatest common divisor and use it to identify the largest common factor or piece length.
questions.question: Two ribbons are \(90\text{ cm}\) and \(150\text{ cm}\) long. They are cut into equal pieces of the greatest possible length, with nothing left over. What is the length of each piece?
questions.explanation: Factor \(90=2\times 3^2\times 5\) and \(150=2\times 3\times 5^2\). Taking the lowest shared exponents gives \(2\times 3\times 5=30\). Both ribbons can be cut into pieces of this length. The value \(15\) also divides both lengths but is not the greatest possible common length.
questions.hint: The piece length must divide both ribbon lengths; look for the greatest common divisor.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the greatest common divisor and use it to identify the largest common factor or piece length.
questions.question: What is the greatest common divisor of \(144\) and \(180\)?
questions.explanation: Write \(144=2^4\times 3^2\) and \(180=2^2\times 3^2\times 5\). The common prime factors are \(2\) and \(3\). Taking the lowest power of each gives \(2^2\times 3^2=4\times 9=36\). Therefore, the greatest common divisor is \(36\). The alternative \(72\) is not a divisor of every given integer.
questions.hint: Use prime factorization and multiply the common prime factors with the smallest exponents.
